description: M2 the transfer money path plus the HTTP app skeleton it needs, and the isolation lab. Single-transaction transfer: lock both accounts FOR UPDATE ordered ascending by id, re-read under lock, reject insufficient (amount+fee), write balanced ledger entries, update stored balances, audit, commit at READ COMMITTED. Includes Express app wiring (request_id, uniform errors, zod validation), users/wallets create routes, the three money POSTs (top-up/peer/withdraw) WITHOUT idempotency yet (added in FEAT-004) and WITHOUT fraud (added in FEAT-005), balance + paginated statement reads, server.ts entrypoint, docs/isolation.md, and the stampede acceptance test. Depends on FEAT-002 (schema).
steps: Create src/http/requestId.ts (assign req.request_id = client-supplied or new UUID) and src/http/errors.ts (AppError class carrying {code, httpStatus, message}; an Express error middleware that renders the uniform shape {code, message, request_id}; the full error catalogue from design §8: VALIDATION_ERROR, INVALID_AMOUNT, UNSUPPORTED_CURRENCY, SAME_WALLET, MISSING_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY, IDEMPOTENCY_BODY_MISMATCH(422), INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS(422), NOT_FOUND(404), WALLET_FROZEN/TRANSFER_NOT_HELD(409), RECON_LOCKED(409), UNSUPPORTED_QUESTION(422), INTERNAL(500)).

Create src/http/validation.ts: zod schemas for each body per design §8 (name/email/phone; amount via money.parseAmount; currency=INR; from_wallet_id/to_wallet_id positive ints with from==to -> SAME_WALLET; note <=500; limit 1-100 default 50; offset>=0; question 1-1000). Validation failure maps to the specific 400 code.

Create src/services/auditService.ts (write an audit_log row for a transfer status change: transfer_id, old_status, new_status, actor, now) and src/services/userService.ts + src/services/walletService.ts (create user; create user wallet account is_system=false currency INR balance 0; resolve wallet/account by id with NOT_FOUND).

Create src/services/transferService.ts implementing design §9.1 steps for all three flows (top_up: cash_in->wallet; peer_transfer: wallet->wallet with optional fee from config.fee_paise; withdrawal: wallet->cash_out) as ONE withTransaction at READ COMMITTED: resolve accounts; SELECT id,balance,is_system FROM accounts WHERE id = ANY($1) ORDER BY id FOR UPDATE with the id array pre-sorted ascending; re-read balances under lock; reject if source.balance < amount+fee -> INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS (rollback); insert transfers row (COMPLETED); insert balanced ledger_entries (debit source + credit dest, plus second debit sender + credit fee_revenue when fee>0); UPDATE stored balances; audit NULL->COMPLETED; COMMIT. Leave a clearly-marked seam/hook where idempotency (FEAT-004 step 3) and fraud evaluation (FEAT-005) will insert, so those FEATs extend this method rather than rewrite it. Expose a result object the routes serialize (amounts as strings).

Create src/http/routes/users.ts (POST /users, POST /users/{id}/wallets), src/http/routes/wallets.ts (POST /wallets/{id}/top-up, POST /wallets/{id}/withdraw, GET /wallets/{id}/balance), src/http/routes/transfers.ts (POST /transfers), and src/http/routes/statement.ts (GET /wallets/{id}/statement?limit&offset ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC; GET /wallets/{id}/statement/cursor?limit&cursor keyset on (created_at,id) returning next_cursor as opaque base64). Create src/services/statementService.ts for the read queries. All responses carry request_id and serialize money as strings.

Create src/http/app.ts wiring express.json(), requestId middleware, all routers, and the error middleware last. Create src/server.ts: build pool from env, runMigrations, then app.listen(PORT) (do not listen until migrations complete).

Author docs/isolation.md per design §9.3: a two-psql-session lab with realistic, labeled Session A / Session B command transcripts and observed/expected output demonstrating (a) READ COMMITTED seeing another session's committed change mid-transaction, (b) REPEATABLE READ stable snapshot, (c) SERIALIZABLE aborting with 40001 on write-skew, (d) REPEATABLE READ with a join showing snapshot stability across joined tables.

Create test/integration/stampede.test.ts (AC-1): per iteration, create a user+wallet, top it up to 50000 paise, DISABLE velocity and rapid_drain for the run (set enabled=false or thresholds>100), fire 100 concurrent 1000-paise withdrawals via Promise.all with distinct idempotency keys, assert exactly 50 succeed, wallet ends at 0, balance never negative at any read, and global SUM(debit)=SUM(credit). Repeat ~20 iterations. (Idempotency keys here depend on FEAT-004; if run before FEAT-004 lands, the withdraw route may not yet require a key — the fixer/convergence step reconciles ordering. Mark in findings if the test is authored but the money POSTs do not yet enforce keys.)

Create test/integration/pagination.test.ts (AC-14): seed several transfers for a wallet; assert OFFSET pagination ordering created_at DESC, id DESC and that the cursor endpoint returns the same ordering with a stable keyset cursor across pages.
acceptance_criteria: Against a real Postgres: the stampede test (AC-1) yields exactly 50 successful 1000-paise withdrawals from a 50000 wallet each of ~20 iterations, wallet ends at 0, never negative, debits==credits globally.
Pagination (AC-14) returns correctly ordered rows for both OFFSET and cursor endpoints.
docs/isolation.md exists with the four labeled two-session scenarios and observed output.
Every error response is the uniform {code, message, request_id} shape.
verification: If Postgres reachable: npm run migrate then npx vitest run test/integration/stampede.test.ts test/integration/pagination.test.ts -> pass (stampede is the primary STEP-4 acceptance test).
If no Postgres in-environment: record in findings that the money-path integration tests were authored but NOT executed (no Postgres), and confirm tsc is clean. Do NOT fabricate a stampede pass.
findings:
COMPLETED (code+tests authored and typecheck-verified; Postgres-dependent money-path integration tests authored but NOT executed — no Postgres here).

- `tsc --noEmit` -> EXIT 0, zero errors (all new src/http, src/services, src/server.ts, and both new integration tests compile under strict + noUncheckedIndexedAccess + exactOptionalPropertyTypes).

Invoked via `node node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc` and `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs` because the PowerShell execution policy blocks the npm.ps1/npx.ps1 shims (same as FEAT-001/002).

HONESTY NOTE (no Postgres here): Docker and psql are NOT on PATH. The stampede (AC-1) and pagination (AC-14) integration tests were AUTHORED and TYPECHECKED but NEVER executed against a real Postgres. No stampede/pagination pass is claimed. With a real DATABASE_URL + migrated DB they will run (CI postgres:15 service, or local Postgres).

DEP ADDED: devDependency @types/uuid@^9.0.8 (uuid v9 ships no bundled types; needed by src/http/requestId.ts). Installed via `node .../npm-cli.js install --save-dev` (ps shim blocked).

BUILD-PATH RECONCILIATION (resolves the FEAT-001 findings note): tsconfig keeps rootDir='.' with include src/scripts/test, so tsc emits dist/src/server.js (NOT dist/server.js). Updated package.json start:api/start:worker, Dockerfile CMD, and docker-compose api/worker commands to `node dist/src/server.js` / `node dist/src/worker.js` (option (b) from FEAT-001). migrateRunner resolves ../../migrations from dist/src/db/ which stays correct. NOTE: src/worker.ts is created in FEAT-005; compose already references dist/src/worker.js.

TRANSFERSERVICE SEAM SIGNATURES (src/services/transferService.ts) that FEAT-004/FEAT-005 EXTEND (do not rewrite):
- `executeTransfer(pool: Pool, ctx: TransferContext): Promise<TransferResult>` — ONE withTransaction at READ COMMITTED. Steps follow design §9.1 1-12 with numbered comment markers.
- `TransferType = 'top_up' | 'peer_transfer' | 'withdrawal'`.
- `TransferContext { type: TransferType; fromAccountId: bigint; toAccountId: bigint; amount: bigint; note?: string; actor: string; idempotency?: IdempotencyContext }`.
- `IdempotencyContext { userId: bigint; key: string; bodyHash: string }` — the FEAT-004 carrier (optional today).
- `TransferResult { transfer_id: string; status: 'COMPLETED'|'HELD'; type: TransferType; amount: string; fee: string; wallet_balance: string }` — money as strings.
- FEAT-004 SEAM: private `insertIdempotencyKeyFirst(client, idempotency)` is called as the FIRST in-txn write when ctx.idempotency is set (design §9.1 step 3). Today a no-op. FEAT-004 fills the body (INSERT ... 'in_progress'; on 23505 -> replay path) and the step-11 'mark completed' hook. Replay must be detected ONLY by the UNIQUE(user_id,key) violation — never SELECT an in_progress key.
- FEAT-005 SEAM: private `evaluateFraud(client, ctx, fee): Promise<{decision:'proceed'} | {decision:'hold'; ruleName}>` runs AFTER the funds check, BEFORE ledger writes, under the FOR UPDATE locks (design §9.1 step 6). Today always 'proceed'. The 'hold' branch structure (insert transfers HELD, audit NULL->HELD, commit with ZERO ledger entries, no balance change) is already in place for FEAT-005 to populate risk_flags + rule evaluation.
- Fee: readFeePaise(client) reads config('fee_paise'), defaults 0; applied to peer_transfer ONLY; charged to the sender as a SECOND debit on source + credit to fee_revenue (design §9.1.2). amount+fee is the outflow checked at step 5.
- Lock step: lockAccountsAscending sorts [from,to] ascending and SELECT ... WHERE id = ANY($1) ORDER BY id FOR UPDATE.

SUPPORTING SERVICES:
- src/services/walletService.ts: `createWallet(pool, userId: bigint)`, `getAccount(pool, id: bigint)`, `getAccountOnClient(client, id)`, `getSystemAccount(client, 'cash_in'|'cash_out'|'fee_revenue')`. AccountRecord { id, user_id, is_system, system_type, currency, balance } (balance stays a string from pg INT8 parser).
- src/services/userService.ts: `createUser(pool, {name,email,phone})` -> UserRecord; unique-violation (23505) -> VALIDATION_ERROR.
- src/services/auditService.ts: `writeTransferAudit(client, {transferId, oldStatus, newStatus, actor})` — same-txn write.
- src/services/statementService.ts: `getStatementOffset(pool, accountId, limit, offset)` and `getStatementCursor(pool, accountId, limit, cursor?)`. Both ORDER BY le.created_at DESC, le.id DESC. Cursor is opaque base64 of {c:created_at, i:entry_id}; keyset predicate (le.created_at, le.id) < ($ts, $id). StatementItem { entry_id, transfer_id, direction, amount, created_at, transfer_type, transfer_status, note, counterparty_account_id }.

HTTP SKELETON:
- src/http/requestId.ts: `requestId` middleware honours valid-UUID X-Request-Id else mints uuid v4; sets req.request_id and X-Request-Id response header. (src/http/types.ts augments Express.Request with request_id.)
- src/http/errors.ts: `AppError(code, message)` with httpStatus from the full §8 catalogue; `errorMiddleware` (register LAST) renders uniform {code, message, request_id}; unknown throws -> opaque INTERNAL 500. ErrorCode union = VALIDATION_ERROR, INVALID_AMOUNT, UNSUPPORTED_CURRENCY, SAME_WALLET, MISSING_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY, IDEMPOTENCY_BODY_MISMATCH(422), INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS(422), NOT_FOUND(404), WALLET_FROZEN(409), TRANSFER_NOT_HELD(409), RECON_LOCKED(409), UNSUPPORTED_QUESTION(422), INTERNAL(500).
- src/http/validation.ts: zod schemas createUserSchema, createWalletSchema, amountBodySchema, transferSchema, idParamSchema, statementQuerySchema, cursorQuerySchema, askSchema; `parseOrThrow<S extends z.ZodTypeAny>(schema, data): z.output<S>` maps failures to the SPECIFIC code via branded sentinels (amount->INVALID_AMOUNT, currency->UNSUPPORTED_CURRENCY, from==to->SAME_WALLET, else VALIDATION_ERROR). amount delegates to money.parseAmount and additionally rejects 0.
- src/http/app.ts: `createApp(pool): Express` wires express.json() -> requestId -> /health -> users/wallets/transfers/statement routers -> errorMiddleware LAST. FEAT-005 mounts admin router, FEAT-006 adds statement/ask — both before errorMiddleware.
- src/server.ts: loadConfig -> createPool -> runMigrations (await to completion) -> app.listen(PORT). Never listens before migrations finish.

ROUTE SHAPES later FEATs extend (all responses carry request_id; money as strings):
- POST /users {name,email,phone} -> 201 {id,name,email,phone,kyc_status,request_id}. Idempotency-exempt.
- POST /users/:id/wallets {currency:'INR'} -> 201 {id,user_id,currency,balance,request_id}. Idempotency-exempt.
- POST /wallets/:id/top-up {amount} -> 201 {transfer_id,status,wallet_balance,request_id}. cash_in->wallet. Path wallet must be a USER wallet (system path wallet -> NOT_FOUND). FEAT-004 adds Idempotency-Key requirement (NOT enforced yet — see note below).
- POST /wallets/:id/withdraw {amount} -> 201 {transfer_id,status,wallet_balance,request_id}. wallet->cash_out. FEAT-004 adds key requirement.
- POST /transfers {from_wallet_id,to_wallet_id,amount,note?} -> 201 {transfer_id,status,type,amount,fee,wallet_balance,request_id}. Both sides must be USER wallets. actor = owner of from_wallet_id. FEAT-004 adds key requirement.
- GET /wallets/:id/balance -> 200 {wallet_id,balance,request_id}.
- GET /wallets/:id/statement?limit&offset -> 200 {items,limit,offset,request_id}.
- GET /wallets/:id/statement/cursor?limit&cursor -> 200 {items,next_cursor,request_id}.
- GET /health -> 200 {status:'ok',request_id}.

IDEMPOTENCY ORDERING NOTE (FEAT-004 reconciles): per design §8 the three money POSTs (top-up/transfers/withdraw) will REQUIRE an Idempotency-Key. FEAT-003 ships them WITHOUT key enforcement (the seam is wired but inert); the stampede test already sends distinct Idempotency-Key headers per request so it keeps passing once FEAT-004 makes the header mandatory. FEAT-004 adds src/http/idempotency.ts, wires it into the three routes (400 MISSING_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY before DB work), and populates ctx.idempotency so insertIdempotencyKeyFirst/step-11 become live.

TESTS:
- test/integration/stampede.test.ts (AC-1): ~20 iterations; per iteration create user+wallet, top up to 50000 paise via a balanced top_up, DISABLE velocity+rapid_drain for the run (restored in afterAll), fire 100 concurrent 1000-paise withdrawals through the REAL HTTP app (app.listen(0) + fetch) with distinct Idempotency-Key headers, assert exactly 50 x 201 and 50 x 422 INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS, no success reports a negative balance, wallet ends at 0; after the run assert global SUM(debit)=SUM(credit) over ledger_entries.
- test/integration/pagination.test.ts (AC-14): seed 25 top_up transfers with strictly-increasing created_at; assert OFFSET pages are ordered created_at DESC, id DESC and tile the full set; assert cursor pagination walks the identical ordering with a stable keyset cursor.
